info.description:
Public Telegram channel data over plain HTTP. No phone number, no api_id, no MTProto client, no session files — one RapidAPI key and you are reading.

**What you get per call**

- Channel facts: member count, description, creation date, verification and boost state.
- The feed with the numbers that matter: every post carries `views` and `forwards`, so engagement is a division, not a research project.
- Cursor pagination over the whole history, with `count` telling you how far it goes.
- Similar-channel recommendations, ready to render as a block.
- Public directory search, stories, replies and discussion threads: 19 routes in one spec.

**Built for people who tried the alternatives.** Telethon and Pyrogram want a phone number, an api_id and a session you have to keep alive. The Bot API only sees channels your bot already administers. Scraping t.me previews breaks with the next markup change.

The free plan is 2,500 calls a month, no card.

**Errors** come back in one envelope with a stable machine-readable `code`, so you write one error path. Every example below is a real response, measured 2026-09-16.
info.title: tgAtlas — Telegram Channel Data API
info.summary: Read any public Telegram channel from your code: size, feed, per-post views and forwards.

CursorQuery.description: Opaque pagination cursor obtained from `next_page` or `prev_page` in a previous response. Overrides `offset_id` and `limit` when supplied. Fails with 400 if tampered with.
CursorQuery.name: cursor

LimitQuery.description: Maximum items to return. Defaults to 20 when omitted; values above 100 are clamped to 100.
LimitQuery.name: limit

MsgIDPath.description: Numeric message id within the given peer. Obtain from a prior `/v1/peers/{peer_id}/history` response.
MsgIDPath.name: msg_id

PeerIDPath.description: Numeric Telegram peer id (channel or user). Obtain from `/v1/usernames/{username}`, `/v1/phones/{phone}`, `/v1/contacts/search`, or any prior response's `peer.user_id` / `peer.channel_id` field.
PeerIDPath.name: peer_id

BadRequest.description: Invalid request — bad path or query parameter.

ResourceUnavailable.description: The peer id could not be found, so no access hash exists for it. Not transient: seed the id via GET /v1/usernames/{username}, GET /v1/phones/{phone}, or by encountering it in a chat, then retry. Raw MTProto ids only: a Bot-API id like -1001234567890 must be sent as 1234567890 (strip the leading -100), and -123456789 as 123456789. When the request carries such an id, the hint names the exact id to retry with.

ChannelDetails.description: Get-full-channel envelope. `full_chat` carries the extended profile; `chats[0]` carries the regular chat record for cross-reference.

ChannelParticipants.description: Channel/supergroup members matching the requested filter.

count.description: Total participant count matching the filter.

ChannelsBatch.description: Batch channels fetch result. Channels that could not be resolved appear in `skipped[]` instead of `chats[]`.

skipped.description: Channel ids that could not be resolved.

ChannelsList.description: Wrapper carrying a `chats[]` list. Used by channel-recommendations.

Chat.description: Telegram chat record. Covers legacy groups, channels, and supergroups; the boolean flags `broadcast`, `megagroup`, and `gigagroup` disambiguate the variant.

broadcast.description: True if this is a broadcast channel.

date.description: Unix timestamp the chat was created.

fake.description: True if Telegram has flagged this chat as fake.

forum.description: True if this is a forum (channel with topics).

gigagroup.description: True if this is a gigagroup (broadcast-only supergroup).

id.description: Chat peer id. Pass this as `peer_id` to channel/peer endpoints.

join_request.description: True if join requires admin approval.

left.description: True if the viewer has left this chat.

megagroup.description: True if this is a supergroup.

min.description: True if the record is a stripped (min) representation.

noforwards.description: True if content protection (no forwards) is enabled.

participants_count.description: Approximate participant count (may be 0 if not exposed).

restricted.description: True if this chat is restricted (see `restriction_reason`).

scam.description: True if Telegram has flagged this chat as a scam.

signatures.description: True if posts show their author.

slowmode_enabled.description: True if slow mode is on.

title.description: Public display title of the chat.

usernames.description: All public usernames bound to this chat.

verified.description: True if Telegram has verified this chat.

ChatFull.description: Extended chat/channel profile. Returned inside `full_chat` of the get-full-channel envelope.

boosts_applied.description: Number of boosts applied to the channel.

bot_info.description: Bot descriptions for bots in this chat.

call.description: Active group call descriptor, null if no call.

can_delete_channel.description: True if the channel may be deleted.

can_set_stickers.description: True if a sticker set may be assigned.

can_set_username.description: True if the username is editable.

can_view_revenue.description: True if monetisation stats are exposed.

hidden_prehistory.description: True if history is hidden from new members.

id.description: Chat peer id (matches the Chat.id in the same response).

linked_chat_id.description: Linked discussion chat id (for broadcast channels with a comments group).

slowmode_next_send_date.description: Unix timestamp of the next allowed post under slow mode.

slowmode_seconds.description: Slow-mode interval in seconds, 0 if disabled.

unread_count.description: Unread message count for the viewer.

ContactsSearch.description: Hybrid contact + global directory search. `results[]` are public directory matches; `my_results[]` is reserved for future use and is currently null.

DiscussionMessage.description: Resolved discussion thread root for a channel post. `messages[]` are the thread root(s).

max_id.description: Latest reply message id in the thread.

read_inbox_max_id.description: Latest incoming reply read by the viewer.

read_outbox_max_id.description: Latest outgoing reply read by the viewer.

Error.description: Error envelope returned by all non-2xx responses.

hint.description: Optional recovery hint suggesting a concrete next call. Set on RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (how to seed an unknown peer id) and SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.
hint.example: retry shortly, or call /v1/usernames/{username} or /v1/peers/{peer_id}/history first.

Message.description: Telegram message. Appears in history, replies, channel-message-by-id, and search responses.

edit_date.description: Unix timestamp of the last edit, or 0 if never edited.

entities.description: Inline message entities (bold, mention, url, etc.).

from_id.description: Sender peer. Null for channel posts (where the channel itself is the author).

fwd_from.description: Forwarded-from envelope. Present only if the message was forwarded.

grouped_id.description: Album group id; messages with the same value belong to one album.

media.description: Attached media (photo / video / document / poll / webpage). Shape varies by type.

media_unread.description: True if the media is unread.

mentioned.description: True if the viewer is mentioned in this message.

out.description: True if the message was outgoing from the viewer's perspective.

post.description: True if this is a channel post (rather than a chat message).

post_author.description: Display name of the post's author (signed broadcasts).

replies.description: Reply thread summary (count, latest reply id). 0 replies if no discussion.

reply_markup.description: Inline keyboard / reply markup, if attached.

reply_to.description: Reply / thread reference. Present only if the message is a reply.

silent.description: True if the message was sent without notification.

MessagesEnvelope.description: Messages list with related chats/users. Used by history, replies, and channel-messages-by-id endpoints.

count.description: Total number of messages matching the query (may exceed the returned page).

next_page.description: Opaque cursor for the next (older) page. Pass back as `?cursor=`. Absent when no further page exists.

offset_id_offset.description: Absolute position of `messages[0]` in the full result set.

prev_page.description: Opaque cursor for the previous (newer) page. Pass back as `?cursor=`. Absent when already on the first page.

topics.description: Forum topics referenced by the messages, if the chat is a forum.

Peer.description: Telegram peer reference. Exactly one of `user_id`, `chat_id`, or `channel_id` is set, identifying the peer type.

channel_id.description: Set when this peer is a channel or supergroup.

chat_id.description: Set when this peer is a legacy basic group chat.

user_id.description: Set when this peer is a user (1:1 chat partner or contact).

PeerStories.description: Currently active stories for a peer.

Photo.description: Photo metadata. The image bytes are not returned; clients fetch them out-of-band.

dcid.description: Telegram data-center id where the photo lives.

has_video.description: True if the photo has a video preview.

stripped_thumb.description: Base64-ish stripped JPEG thumbnail; can be expanded client-side.

ResolvedPeer.description: Result of a username or phone lookup. Pass `peer.user_id`/`peer.channel_id` to subsequent endpoints to fetch full data.

chats.description: Chat records resolved alongside the peer; may be null when only a cache reference was returned.

users.description: User records resolved alongside the peer; may be null when only a cache reference was returned.

StoriesByID.description: Specific stories fetched by id for a peer. Story media file references are downloadable via GET /v1/files/{file_id}.

User.description: Telegram user record. Appears in `users[]` arrays of nearly every response.

bot.description: True if this account is a bot.

deleted.description: True if the account has been deleted.

fake.description: True if Telegram has flagged this account as fake.

first_name.description: First name (may be empty for deleted accounts).

id.description: User peer id. Pass this as `peer_id` to `/v1/users/{peer_id}`.

lang_code.description: BCP-47-ish locale code reported by the client (e.g. "en", "ru").

mutual_contact.description: True if the contact relationship is mutual.

phone.description: Phone number in international format. Empty unless the caller has visibility.

photo.description: Profile photo metadata. Null if no photo is set.

premium.description: True if this account has Telegram Premium.

restricted.description: True if this user is restricted (see `restriction_reason`).

restriction_reason.description: Reasons for any restriction. Null when not restricted.

scam.description: True if Telegram has flagged this account as a scam.

status.description: Online status object (varies by privacy settings).

username.description: Primary public @username (empty if the user has none).

usernames.description: All public usernames bound to this user (some accounts collect multiple).

verified.description: True if Telegram has verified this user.

UserDetails.description: Get-full-user envelope. `full_user` carries the extended profile; `users[0]` carries the regular user record for cross-reference.

UserFull.description: Extended user profile. Returned inside `full_user` of the get-full-user envelope.

about.description: Bio text shown on the profile.

blocked.description: True if the viewer has blocked this user.

bot_info.description: Bot metadata. Present when the user is a bot.

common_chats_count.description: Number of chats this user shares with the viewer.

contact_require_premium.description: True if only premium users may DM this account.

fallback_photo.description: Fallback profile photo shown to users who lack access to the primary one.

has_scheduled.description: True if scheduled messages exist with this peer.

id.description: User peer id (matches the User.id in the same response).

personal_channel_id.description: Linked personal channel id, if any.

personal_channel_message.description: Featured message id in the personal channel.

phone_calls_available.description: True if the user accepts phone calls.

phone_calls_private.description: True if call privacy is engaged.

pinned_msg_id.description: Pinned message id, or 0 if no pin.

settings.description: Per-peer settings (report buttons, contact requests, etc.).

sponsored_enabled.description: True if sponsored messages are enabled.

translations_disabled.description: True if message translation is opt-out for this peer.

video_calls_available.description: True if video calls are available.

voice_messages_forbidden.description: True if the user rejects voice messages.

UserPhotos.description: Profile photo history for a user. `count` is present only when the result is paginated (PhotosPhotosSlice).

count.description: Total photo count when paginated. Absent when the full set is returned.

UsernameAlias.description: One public username alias bound to a user or chat.

active.description: True if the alias is currently active.

editable.description: True if the alias can be edited (only true for the primary one).

get.summary: Fetch specific channel messages by id

get.description:
Members of a public **group (megagroup)**, paginated.

**Precondition.** Telegram exposes member lists for groups, not for broadcast channels: check `full_chat.can_view_participants` from `GET /v1/channels/{peer_id}` first. `true` means this call returns the list; `false` means it answers `404 NOT_FOUND`, which is Telegram's rule rather than an outage. Discussion groups linked to a channel (`full_chat.linked_chat_id`) normally do allow it.

Use `filter` to narrow the list — `recent` (default), `admins`, `bots`, `kicked`, `banned`, or `search` together with `q`. `limit` defaults to 20 and is clamped to 100. Resolve a `@username` with `/v1/usernames/{username}` first to get the numeric `peer_id`.

parameters.description: One of `recent` (default), `admins`, `bots`, `kicked`, `banned`, `search`. `kicked`/`banned`/`search` use `q`.
parameters.name: filter

parameters.description: Search query, used by the `kicked`/`banned`/`search` filters.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Number of participants to skip.
parameters.name: offset

get.description:
Returns matching peers from the public directory.

`q` must be at least 4 characters: Telegram's directory search ignores shorter queries and answers with an empty result rather than an error, so this API rejects them up front (400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, `query too short`) instead of returning an empty page you would have to interpret.

A shorter term still works if you pad it to four characters with spaces: `?q=gta%20` searches for `gta` and returns GTA-prefixed peers. Telegram measures the query as sent but trims it before matching, and `q` is forwarded to it byte-for-byte.

parameters.description: Search query — username substring, full name, or phone fragment. Minimum 4 characters as sent; pad a shorter term with spaces (`gta%20`). Telegram returns nothing for shorter queries.
parameters.name: q

get.summary: Search Telegram contacts and the public directory

get.description: Streams the bytes of a file referenced by `file_id`. The id is obtained from a prior message, channel, or user response (look for `media.photo.id` or `media.document.id` in `/v1/peers/{peer_id}/history`, or `photo.id` on a user / channel profile). For photo files, an explicit `thumb_size` may be requested; if omitted, the largest available size is returned.

parameters.description: Numeric file id obtained from a prior response (e.g. `media.photo.id`, `media.document.id`). File ids exceed 2^53, so a JSON parser that reads numbers as doubles (`JSON.parse` in JavaScript, among others) will silently round them. Read id fields as strings or big integers — from the raw response body — or the id you send back will not be the one we returned. A rounded id is repaired automatically when it names exactly one file we have seen; when several files round to the same value the response is 409 and you should add `peer_id` and `msg_id`.
parameters.name: file_id

parameters.description: Peer the file was seen in. Optional; used only to disambiguate a `file_id` that lost precision in your JSON parser.
parameters.name: peer_id

parameters.description: Message the file was seen in. Optional; used with `peer_id` to disambiguate a `file_id` that lost precision in your JSON parser.
parameters.name: msg_id

parameters.description: Photo files only: requested thumbnail size code (e.g. `s`, `m`, `x`, `y`). Omit to receive the largest available size. Ignored for documents.
parameters.name: thumb_size

200.description: File bytes streamed as a binary response. `Content-Type` reflects the file's media type when known, otherwise `application/octet-stream`.

get.description: Resolves a query against Telegram's public directory and returns the matching **entities** (`users`, `chats`, `results`) — the same response shape as `GET /v1/contacts/search`, which is the route to use directly in new integrations. `q` and `limit` are forwarded; `offset_id` and `cursor` are ignored. Kept in place so existing integrations keep working unchanged.

parameters.description: Search query (forwarded to the public-directory search). Minimum 4 characters as sent; pad a shorter term with spaces (`gta%20`).
parameters.name: q

400.description: Missing or blank `q`, or a `q` shorter than 4 characters.

parameters.description: Return messages with `id < offset_id`. Ignored when `cursor` is supplied.
parameters.name: offset_id

parameters.description: Return messages strictly older than this Unix timestamp.
parameters.name: offset_date

parameters.description: Items to skip relative to `offset_id`. Negative values shift toward newer messages.
parameters.name: add_offset

parameters.description: Return messages with `id < max_id`.
parameters.name: max_id

parameters.description: Return messages with `id > min_id`.
parameters.name: min_id

parameters.description: Cache-busting hash; leave 0 unless you are reusing a prior result.
parameters.name: hash

get.description:
Returns the root message of a channel post's linked discussion thread. Fails with 404 if the post has no discussion thread.

**Precondition.** Only posts with comments enabled have a thread. In `GET /v1/peers/{peer_id}/history` each message carries `replies.comments`: `true` means this call returns the thread, `false` means 404 `NOT_FOUND`. A channel without a linked discussion group (`full_chat.linked_chat_id` = 0) never has one.

get.description: Active stories of a public channel or user. Answers `200` with a `stories` object for the peer; when nothing is live at that moment its inner `stories` field is `null` rather than an array, so read it as "no active stories" and not as an error (measured 16 September 2026 on channel id 1006503122). Story ids from this list stay resolvable afterwards through `GET /v1/peers/{peer_id}/stories/{ids}`. Resolve a `@username` with `/v1/usernames/{username}` first to get the numeric `peer_id`.

Specific stories of a peer by id. `ids` is a comma-separated list of story ids (for example `1,2,3`), and the answer carries `count` plus the matching story objects with caption, entities, date and media. Ids are permanent: a request for `1,2,3` on channel id 1006503122 returned `count: 3` including a story posted 3 December 2023, so archived stories remain readable long after the 24-hour window in which they are "active" (measured 16 September 2026). An id nobody posted answers `200` with `count: 0` and `stories: null`; a list that cannot be parsed answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST`. Story media file references are downloadable via `GET /v1/files/{file_id}`. Resolve a `@username` with `/v1/usernames/{username}` first to get the numeric `peer_id`.

parameters.description: Comma-separated list of story ids (e.g. `42,41`). Maximum 100.
parameters.name: ids
